source.rationale: New change-type category not covered by cases 001-007: a parameter RENAME (chunk_size -> block_size), same default, same position -- distinct from addition (001/006), removal (007), and default-value-only change (018/019). The doc's example call and parameter bullet both still use the old name, which after the rename is not just incomplete but actively wrong (a reader copying the example gets a TypeError).

stale_doc_section:
```python
read_stream(f, chunk_size=4096)
```

* `chunk_size` -- number of bytes to read at a time. Defaults to `8192`.
human_fixed_doc_section:
```python
read_stream(f, block_size=4096)
```

* `block_size` -- number of bytes to read at a time. Defaults to `8192`.

labels.notes_for_labeler: CONFIRMED (real run), NEW FINDING for FPO #11. applied_old_text/proposed_new_text show the corrector fixed ONLY the parameter bullet ('`chunk_size`' -> '`block_size`') -- the code example (`read_stream(f, chunk_size=4096)`) was left untouched and will now raise TypeError if run as-is, since chunk_size no longer exists as a keyword argument. Validator approved anyway despite the still-broken example remaining in doc_section (Entry 27: validator receives the full doc_section, not just the span -- it had the information to catch this and didn't). This is the FIRST confirmed instance of the single-span completeness gap on a RENAME change, not just an addition (001, 006, 024, 025) -- meaningful because a rename's leftover stale example is actively broken (TypeError), not just incomplete, which is a more severe real-world consequence than the addition cases' leftover examples (which still run, just without demonstrating the new capability).
